# play-forge
Fun mini-games to play with friends: solo, on one device, or online. No accounts, no server.

**Online with friends:** click **Create room** and share the 5-letter code or the invite link. Opening the link joins the room straight away; players set their name, avatar and character in the room.

**Offline:** `npm run build`, then open `dist/games/<game>/index.html`. Each game is one self-contained HTML file.

## Features

- **Multiplayer, direct first:** browsers connect directly over WebRTC ([Trystero](https://github.com/dmotz/trystero)), with a small relay server as the fallback when networks block that. See [How multiplayer works](#how-multiplayer-works).
- **In every online room:** avatars, emoji reactions, text chat (press **Enter**) and voice chat (open mic or hold **V** to talk). After a reload or reopening the room link, you rejoin voice with the mic muted or not as before (automatically once the mic is allowed, otherwise tap 🎤; remembered for 6 hours in `play-forge:voice-room:<game>:<room>`). Shuttle Pop: hold **T** for a reaction wheel.
- **Host controls:** the host can remove a player with the ✕ on their seat (confirmed in the room). Their seat frees at once, also mid-match; they can join again with the code.
- **English and Vietnamese**, generated music and sounds, and a phone-friendly layout.

## How multiplayer works

```
 Browser A (host) ◄──── direct WebRTC connection ────► Browser B
     ▲     ▲                                              ▲     ▲
     │     └── public Nostr relays (only to find each other) ──┘     │
     └──────── game relay server (fallback, wss://relay.haonguyen.dev) ┘
```

- **Direct first:** players find each other through public relays, then talk directly, browser to browser. The relays are pinned in `engine/net/net-config.ts` (`RELAY_URLS`, with how to re-check them).
- **Relay fallback:** every player also opens a WebSocket to our game relay server (`server/relay`). Messages to a player go directly when that link is up, otherwise through the relay (`engine/net/hybrid.ts`): while WebRTC is still connecting, when a strict network (corporate, some mobile carriers) blocks it, or when a direct link drops mid-game. The relay also lets players find the room if the Nostr relays are down. Voice stays direct only. The relay only forwards messages within a room; the host still runs the game.
  - URL: `VITE_GAME_RELAY_URL` at build time (default `wss://relay.haonguyen.dev`, none on the dev server; empty = no relay, direct only as before).
  - Testing: `?relay=only` sends all game data through the relay, `?relay=off` skips it.
- **Network status:** in an online room, the signal-bars button in the top bar shows connection health (green / yellow / red) and opens a live panel: room code, your role, matchmaking servers, the backup (relay) server, and each player's link (**Direct** or **Via server**, ping). Joining shows each step (servers → room → host) and says which one failed, with **Try again**. Add `?netdebug=1` to log connection and route changes to the console.
- **The host runs the game:** guests send their moves to the host, and the host sends the game state back to everyone.
- **Reconnecting:**
  - A player who reloads or drops keeps their seat for 20 seconds and rejoins automatically.
  - Shuttle Pop 2v2: a leaver who rejoins within the grace window gets their seat back (the computer plays it meanwhile); after it the computer keeps the seat.
  - If the host reloads, the room reopens with the same code and seats. Guests wait up to 30 seconds.
- **Limits:**
  - A host reload ends the current match (the room survives).
  - Keep the host's tab visible, because browsers slow down background tabs.
  - Players who can't connect directly play through the relay: a bit more ping, and no voice between them.

## Develop

```bash
npm install
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5173
npm run check        # typecheck + lint + format + unit tests
npm run test:sim     # long simulation tests (*.simulation.test.ts: balance, bot matches, fairness runs)
npm run test:e2e     # browser tests (first time: npx playwright install chromium)
npm run build        # dist/ (or: npm run build -- snake)
```

Test multiplayer without internet: open a game in two tabs with `?net=local` (voice needs the real network).

Run the game relay locally: `npm run relay` (ws://localhost:8080, allows localhost pages), then build or run the dev server with `VITE_GAME_RELAY_URL=ws://localhost:8080`.

## Project layout

```
engine/      shared library ('@forge'): game shell (app.ts), net, social, audio, ui, fx
games/       one folder per game + games.json (launcher and README table)
launcher/    the game picker page
scripts/     single-file build and README table generator
server/relay game relay server (Node + ws, Docker): fallback path for blocked direct links
```

## Adding a game

1. Copy `games/snake` to `games/<id>/`.
2. Write the rules in `sim.ts` as a `GameDefinition` (`setup`, `tick`, `isFinished`). Keep the state plain JSON.
3. In `main.ts`, call `createGameApp({ def, title, mount, scores, outcome })`. The engine gives you the menus, rooms, social features and sounds.
4. Add `cover.svg` and an entry in `games/games.json`. Put on-screen text through `t()` with a Vietnamese dictionary (see `games/brickstorm/i18n.ts`).

`games/snake` is the reference for rendering, effects and input.

Styles: reuse the shared tokens and components and keep game CSS to what is truly the game's own; see [docs/styling.md](docs/styling.md).

Solo-only games set `maxPlayers: 1`: the start screen then shows just **Play**, with no rooms. Reaction games can reuse `engine/reflex` (difficulty ramp, telegraph timing, timing windows) and `bestScores()` for personal bests (see `games/phantom-drift`). `@forge/reflex/vitals` adds hearts, hit invulnerability, regen and combo multipliers; `@forge/reflex/hud2d` is a ready-made 2D HUD (hearts, score, skill ring with key hint, multiplier, banners), used by Synthstride. Shuttle Pop's personal view settings (camera height/tilt, when the landing ring shows, and the **Flight path**: dots along an incoming shot's predicted flight, `flightpath.ts`, Off / Near drop / Always, off by default; and **Graphics**: Auto / Low / Medium / High, `look.ts` + `quality.ts`; saved in this browser, never sent to the room) are a small camera button at the top-right of the 3D game view, not in the top bar. Shuttle Pop's keyboard is WASD + `Space` (jump) + `Shift` (dive), swinging with the mouse (left button; hold to charge) or the touch button; right-click dives too, and only Esc pauses (`createGameApp({ pauseKeys })`, default Esc + P). Jump and Dive only move the body (`ability.ts` free moves): the player swings in the air / during the dive and that swing uses the move's reach box, so lag rewind and guest prediction share the swing's rules. The dive slides 1.8 m the way you run (never backward), then you run slowed for a moment; the view settings' **Auto swing** (off by default, saved per browser) makes Jump / Dive swing by themselves (the input's `auto` flag). The computer and older clients (no `k`) keep the one-button auto pick (jump-smash, lunge or hop). Shuttle Pop's racket bonk (`stun.ts`): a rally swing whose racket reaches another player (1.2 m beside, 0.85 m across the net) stuns them 0.8 s with 2 s immunity after; the host judges it from current positions after all of a tick's swings, and guests only mirror the lock. The `bonk` event carries the victim as `who` and the swinger as `by` (plus `side`). Shuttle Pop's court size (Normal / Large +15% / XL +30%) is a room option the host sets; the sim keeps the dims in `state.court` (sent to guests) and every rule, shot, the computer, the camera and the park read them from there. `mount()` also gets `{ reactions }` (a `ReactionBridge`): in online rooms a game can send reactions and draw incoming ones in its own view (`draw()`); the shell then only plays the sound (Shuttle Pop's bubbles over the chibis). Games can add their own controls to the start screen with `menuExtras()` (Synthstride's timing calibration), and to an online room's "You" section with `roomExtras()` (Shuttle Pop's character strip; built once per room, so it keeps its own state). An option with `aloneOnly: true` (e.g. the computer's level) hides in a room once a second player sits down. An option's `shownWhen(seated, options)` decides its visibility itself and wins over `aloneOnly` (Shuttle Pop's computer level shows while any seat is empty: alone in 1 vs 1, up to 3 seated in 2 vs 2). `GameDefinition.seating(options)` opts a game into seats and teams: it returns `{ seats, teams, botFill }` for the chosen options (seats clamped to `[minPlayers, maxPlayers]`; default `maxPlayers` seats, one team). Seat `s` plays for team `s % teams`; with teams, the room shows one column per team and players tap **Sit here** to move to a free seat between matches; `botFill` labels empty seats **Computer plays**. Joiners past the seats watch. The host can't switch to a choice with fewer seats than are taken: the room greys it out and says why (`seatsIf`). Shuttle Pop's **Match** option (1 vs 1, the default, or 2 vs 2) uses it: 2 vs 2 opens 4 seats in teams A / B (seats A, B, A, B on join), widens the court to doubles sidelines (3.05 m half-width, court size multiplies on top) and fills every empty seat with the computer (alone: you plus 3 computers), which also takes the seat of a player who leaves mid-match. Doubles serve: the team that wins a point serves; when a team wins the serve back, its other player serves; serve from the right on an even score, the left on odd (`doubles.ts`). Computer teammates split the court (the one nearer the landing takes the shuttle, the other covers), and racket bonks hit teammates too. `session.setProfile(name, avatar)` renames a player from the room (a guest re-sends its hello, so older hosts understand it). Rhythm or timing-critical online games can use `TickClock` (`@forge/net/clock`): a jitter-free local estimate of the host's tick, for scheduling audio and timestamping inputs (Synthstride sends `step@tick:seq` and the host judges and lag-compensates from that). `GameDefinition.netView()` trims host-only data from what guests receive each tick, and `ranking: true` adds a ranked list (plus your own `summary`) to a room's results screen. `leaderboard(state, selfId)` returns a ranked table (`Leaderboard`: stat columns, rows with a colour, an optional badge such as MVP and the local player marked, a note line) shown on solo and room results (Shuttle Pop: points won, Perfect hits, smashes, dive saves and bonks per player, `tally.ts`). Set `music: null` when a game makes its own soundtrack (Synthstride plays its music from the sim's beat events, so it can never drift from the gameplay).

3D games import `@forge/render3d` (three.js scene with bloom and automatic quality drop, HUD overlay, 3D particles, mesh pool). It is kept out of `@forge` so 2D games don't ship three.js. Phantom Drift also shows the pattern of a 2D fallback when WebGL2 is missing. `QualityGovernor` (also exported from `@forge/render3d`) is the frame-time watcher behind the quality drop, for games that trade their own extras. `createScene3D` takes a `levels` ladder (default `QUALITY_LEVELS`); a game's extras ride on `QualityLevel.shadows` and are read via `Scene3D.quality`. Optional extras: `toneMapping` / `exposure`, `ao` (screen-space ambient occlusion, three's GTAO with see-through objects left out, on for levels with `QualityLevel.ao`), `grade` (saturation / contrast / tint in the existing punch pass) and `setLevels()` to swap the ladder live (e.g. a player-picked graphics tier). Shuttle Pop (`look.ts`, all its lighting / shadow / bloom / AO / grade tuning in one place; `quality.ts`): Auto walks High (soft sun shadows from players and park, lamp bloom, grade, AO) → Medium (no AO) → Low (lit scenery, blob shadows only, no post passes), then resolution; a pinned tier only steps resolution; phones on Auto start at Low. The governor waits 2 s after attach, drops on ~2 s of slow frames and probes back up once.

On touch devices, fullscreen gives the game the whole screen: the top bar tucks away behind a small floating handle that brings it back for a few seconds (`engine/ui/fullscreen-chrome.ts`, styles under `.pf-fullscreen` in `shell.css`; a game can move the handle off its own HUD, see `games/brickstorm/brickstorm.css`). Desktops keep the bar. Landscape-only games call `landscapeGuard(stage, onChange)` (`engine/ui/landscape.ts`): a "Rotate your phone" card while a touch phone is upright, plus a landscape lock in fullscreen (`lockLandscape`, released on cleanup); pause or let go of held controls in `onChange` (see `games/shuttle-pop`). A seat that isn't in the lobby (the computer) gets its own colour and avatar on the top-bar score chip by returning `name`, `slot` and `avatar` from `scores()`.

Controls go in `createGameApp({ guide })` as `GuideStep`s (`engine/ui/guide.ts`): rows of keycaps (`keys: [['W', 'A', 'S', 'D'], ['Up', 'Left', 'Down', 'Right']]`, arrows print as glyphs), a mouse icon (`mouse: 'click'`) and a touch icon (`touch: 'button'`), each device seeing only its own rows. The shell adds a Pause row (its `pauseKeys`, default Esc / P), mouse icons name their button (Left click / Right click / Left drag), a "How to play" button on the start, pause and room screens, and pops the card up once before a player's first match (`play-forge:guide-seen:<id>`; solo waits for "Got it", online opens it over the room and closes it when the match starts, so it never holds up a match). A step with `tip: true` is a rule rather than a control (Synthstride's "Step on the beat"): it shows on every device, inputs or not. The older `controls` text still works for games without a guide (see `games/shuttle-pop`).

Heavy setup (building a 3D scene, compiling shaders) goes in `createGameApp({ preload })`: it starts at page load and the start button shows "Loading…" until it's done, so play never freezes on start. Rejoining after a reload and joining from an invite link wait for it too. Before any of that, every built game page paints a splash (its `cover.svg`, title and a loading bar; `scripts/splash.mjs`) while the single-file bundle downloads, and the shell fades it out once its first screen is up. The hub prefetches a game when you hover or touch its card.

## Deploy

Every push to `main` is tested, built and published to GitHub Pages (`.github/workflows/pages.yml`).

The game relay (`server/relay`) is deployed separately, as a Docker container behind a Cloudflare Tunnel (no open ports):

```bash
docker build -f server/relay/Dockerfile -t play-forge-relay .   # from the repo root
```

- Env: `PORT` (8080, WebSocket + `/healthz`), `METRICS_PORT` (9464, Prometheus `/metrics`; keep it off the tunnel), `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (comma-separated page origins), `CLIENT_IP_HEADER` (default `cf-connecting-ip`; only trust it when the tunnel is the sole way in).
- Limits (per room, socket, address and message rate) are in `engine/net/relay-protocol.ts` (`RELAY_LIMITS`). Nothing is stored on disk.
- Clients built before the relay keep working: they just use direct links only. Protocol changes get a new path (`/v2`).

The version shown at the bottom of the launcher is `MAJOR.MINOR.<commit count>` (`scripts/version.mjs`): it goes up by itself with every commit on `main`. Bump `MAJOR.MINOR` in `package.json` for a big release. The dev server shows it with `-dev`.
